item: Every session's record says which memory tier it was resolved to and when: the boot record, the chronology, the crash report and the soak window carry the reading, with the tier the machine would resolve to now beside it
key_paths: src/config/memory_budget.py; src/monitoring/session_history.py; src/monitoring/chronology.py; src/monitoring/session_hwm.py; src/monitoring/forensics.py; src/monitoring/soak_window.py; tests/test_memory_budget_reading.py; docs/ledger/OPEN_QUEUE.md; docs/ledger/LESSONS.md
summary: The in-memory keyword rollup runs on every tier but small, and the 2026-10-06 bundles could not say why it was off on seven of fifteen machines: the tier reached a report only on a pass-end summary line (three of seventeen bundles kept one) and it is resolved once per process from the RAM total read at that instant, which moves on a virtual machine whose memory is ballooned (three machines resolved small and read 4.07, 4.95 and 5.78 GiB at export). memory_budget.resolved_reading() is the reading the cached budget was resolved from (tier, RAM total, nominal size, cores, whether the tier leaves the rollup on, and when) and reading_vs_now() puts it beside what the machine reads now, as two facts and no verdict. The boot record carries the reading, the allocator (compactly) and whether an operator forced the rollup either way; chronology sessions carry them once; the session's high-water header carries the reading into the next boot's report as the previous session's and the crash report prints one line for it beside the peaks it bounds; the soak window carries the pair in every state its guard block can end in. The budget is still resolved once (pinned), now under a lock. Whether to re-resolve is a proposal in OPEN_QUEUE.md, not done, because switching a machine up turns the rollup build on. Twenty-five tests and thirty-three mutations each caught. Lesson: LESSONS.md, A VALUE RESOLVED ONCE FROM A READING THAT CAN MOVE IS A FACT ABOUT AN INSTANT.
